key_insight: An agentic AI workflow could review hospital readmissions with quality ratings similar to physician reviewers while costing far less per chart.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI may help hospitals scale readmission review and surface recurring quality-improvement opportunities without replacing expert oversight.
method: Single-center blinded comparison of 20 unplanned 30-day readmissions from a medicine service
AI agent queried structured clinical data and completed the same readmission-review rubric used by physicians
Expanded exploratory analysis applied the refined workflow to 100 additional recent readmissions
evidence_signal: In the primary evaluation, AI and physicians had similar preventability rates and blinded quality scores, with no hallucinations identified during factuality review, though agreement on preventability was low.
watch_item: Results come from a small single-center study, so generalizability and consistency across settings and reviewers remain uncertain.
paper_title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Hospital Readmission Review: A Single-Center Blinded Evaluation and Exploratory Qualitative Analysis
